reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes joining a team through specified TRX contributions and promises double or triple profits through successive recruitment. The speaker claims that 330 TRX can be recovered within one or two days after obtaining several subscribers, and directs viewers to a description link and contact number for guidance on joining and earning money.

first of all u buy trx i have tell u you are need for level 1 trx if u want for level 2 trx you need 750 trx
And you will also get some things out of money that he will join. It will give you profit. From every point you will get the money.
in next six months you will earn good,25,30 joinings So your 10,20,30 joining will go further then you will get profit
you will recover your 330 TRX you invested within 1 or 2 days I have put in your money in one day by having 3 or 4 subscribers

opening.argument: The presentation does not simply certify an opportunity and demand unquestioning trust. It expressly says the speaker will explain “whether it is fake or real,” and admits, “I'm not an expert.” That framing supports an informational discussion in which viewers are expected to evaluate the platform for themselves. The speaker also presents decentralization as the relevant safety feature, stating that “no admin is involved” and that “no scams and no fraud will happen.” Those statements may be optimistic, but they are still an explicit explanation of the claimed risk basis, not concealment of the subject. The video therefore fits an anti-scam or investigative discussion more plausibly than a deceptive certification.

citations.quote: I'll tell you whether it is fake or real
As I am saying in the video, my website, I'm not an expert.
is a decentralized platform that means no admin is involved no scams and no fraud will happen

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution selects the most promotional-sounding excerpts but does not address the qualifying context: the speaker says the video will determine whether the platform is “fake or real” and acknowledges not being an expert. The cited earnings language therefore cannot, by itself, establish deceptive intent rather than an optimistic explanation of a controversial platform. The supplied material also does not establish that the claimed returns occurred or that viewers were guaranteed payment.

citations.quote: I'll tell you whether it is fake or real
I'm not an expert.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the topic “fake or real” does not withdraw the endorsement that follows. The speaker affirmatively says “no scams and no fraud will happen,” while directing viewers toward joining and earnings. A disclaimer of expertise does not neutralize concrete recruitment and recovery claims. The cited statements show that the promised income is tied to other people joining, not merely to neutral risk analysis.

citations.quote: no scams and no fraud will happen
you will also get some things out of money that he will join. It will give you profit.
you will recover your 330 TRX you invested within 1 or 2 days

opening.argument: The video's stated purpose is explanatory: it says it will discuss what the platform is, how it is earned, its working process, and how withdrawal works, “with detail.” The speaker then says, “Let's go through the steps,” and describes how to use the site. That is the structure of a tutorial or operational demonstration, not necessarily a solicitation disguised as neutral content. The offer to answer questions and explain the process further also supports an instructional role. Even where the speaker describes possible earnings, the central activity presented is teaching viewers how the system is supposed to operate and how to assess or navigate it.

citations.quote: We are going to talk in today's video about what is force edge How is it earned What is the working process and how we get withdrawal
All the things are with detail I will tell you about force edge in this video
So let's go through the steps.
If you have any doubts in comments section I will clear them out

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats instructional detail as proof of a scam, but explaining levels, withdrawal, and the proposed workflow is equally consistent with a tutorial about a digital platform. Its excerpts show what the speaker describes, not that the video presents a false outcome. The speaker explicitly says the process will be explained in detail and invites questions, which is ordinary educational framing.

citations.quote: All the things are with detail I will tell you about force edge in this video
If you have any doubts in comments section I will clear them out

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing does not change what is being taught. The operational steps require joining, purchasing TRX for levels, and recruiting or obtaining subscribers for earnings. The speaker says viewers should join his team and that money comes from another person's joining. That is instruction in a recruitment-income mechanism, not detached education or a neutral demonstration.

citations.quote: If you join my team which has high profile Then you will get double or triple profit
first of all u buy trx i have tell u you are need for level 1 trx
you will also get some things out of money that he will join. It will give you profit.

opening.argument: The supplied material identifies a digital platform and a contact-based service offering guidance, but it does not show a transfer, account credential request, or an independently verified outcome. The description gives a contact number, while the speaker says the team will guide participants, explain where to post, and answer doubts. That is consistent with a referral or coaching service whose exact external operation is not observable here. The prosecution cannot fill that evidentiary gap by treating every mention of joining as proof of fraud. The record does not show the destination behind the description link, nor establish that any promised amount was actually paid or withheld.

citations.quote: My contact number [PHONE]
Our complete team will guide you.
we will all guide you.
Just Simply Just Go To My WhatsApp And Link In The Description And Call Me

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited excerpts identify a platform and prospective guidance, but they do not establish that the speaker collected money, obtained credentials, or controlled a fraudulent payout. Even the contact invitation is not evidence of what the linked destination contains. Without that missing mechanism or a demonstrated loss, the material supports ordinary referral promotion or coaching at least as well as a scam finding.

citations.quote: Our complete team will guide you.
Just Simply Just Go To My WhatsApp And Link In The Description And Call Me

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The mechanism is expressly described: participants buy TRX to unlock levels, join a team, and receive money from other people's joinings. The speaker also predicts recovery of the initial TRX within one or two days after getting subscribers. That is not merely a service contact or ordinary coaching fee; it ties earnings to recruitment and incoming participants. The absent linked page is unnecessary because the video itself supplies the relevant mechanism.
